key_insight: At sufficiently large penalties and long annealing times, penalty-based quantum annealing approaches the same conditional ground-state sampling distribution as constrained quantum annealing.
engineering_relevance: Penalty-based and constraint-preserving implementations can exhibit similar sampling bias despite using different driver Hamiltonians.
method: Simulate closed-system annealing on random graph bipartitioning instances.
Compare conditional ground-state distributions using Jensen–Shannon divergence.
Use degenerate perturbation theory to connect virtual spin flips with the projected XY driver.
evidence_signal: For the studied instances, Jensen–Shannon divergence decreases approximately as the inverse square of the penalty-to-objective energy ratio, consistent with perturbation theory.
watch_item: The correspondence requires the stated perturbative conditions and does not establish uniform sampling or robustness to hardware noise.
paper_title: Ground-State Sampling Correspondence between Penalty-Based and Constrained Quantum Annealing
